card.title: Kirchhoff's laws — current and voltage bookkeeping

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Current is drifting electrons (I = nAev_d — slow drift, fast signal). Ohm's law (V = IR) makes metals linear; filaments and diodes bend the I–V curve (non-ohmic). Kirchhoff's two laws are conservation in disguise: charge at a junction (ΣI = 0), energy around any loop (ΣV = 0). Real batteries add internal resistance r, so terminal voltage sags under load: V = E − Ir.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: I = nAev_d · V = IR, R = ρL/A  ·  series: R = ΣRᵢ · parallel: 1/R = Σ1/Rᵢ  ·  junction: ΣI_in = ΣI_out · loop: Σ(EMF) = Σ(IR)  ·  terminal V = E − Ir  ·  divider: V₁ = V·R₁/(R₁+R₂)  ·  2/3/6 Ω parallel on 12 V: R_eq = 1 Ω, I_total = 12 A

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Ohm's law needs constant temperature (heating bends the line). Kirchhoff holds for lumped DC circuits (no changing magnetic flux through loops). Internal-resistance sag assumes the source model E + r; potential-divider formula needs the same series current (unloaded output).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 2 Ω, 3 Ω, 6 Ω in parallel: 1/R = 1/2+1/3+1/6 = 1 → R = 1 Ω; across 12 V the battery delivers 12 A (NEB 2021). Short circuit: R → 0, current limited only by r. Wheatstone balance (P/Q = R/S) and potentiometer null points are Kirchhoff applications.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 2/3/6 Ω parallel across 12 V (negligible r): conductances add — 1/R = (3+2+1)/6 = 1 → R_eq = 1 Ω; total current I = V/R = 12 A, splitting 6/4/2 A inverse to resistance (NEB 2021, 4 marks). Branch currents rejoin at the junction — Kirchhoff's first law visible.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Kirchhoff's loop law fails with induced EMF (changing flux needs Faraday). Ohm's law fails for non-ohmic devices and at temperature extremes (superconductors: R = 0 below Tc). Drift speed (~mm/s) is not signal speed (~c) — the field, not electrons, races down the wire.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Drift: electrons accelerated by E gain v between collisions every τ; averaging gives v_d = eEτ/m, and I = nAev_d = (ne²τA/mL)·V — the bracket is 1/R, deriving Ohm microscopically with ρ = m/(ne²τ). Loop law: carry a test charge around any closed path back to start — net energy change must be zero (conservative electrostatic field).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Two resistors parallel: R = product/sum. Equal R in parallel: R/n. 'State Kirchhoff' = 5-mark opener (NEB 2022): junction (charge) + loop (energy), then apply to the given circuit. Sag questions: V = E − Ir, find r from two load points.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2022 (5): Kirchhoff's laws + solve a simple circuit. NEB 2021 (4): 2/3/6 Ω parallel on 12 V — total current. Series/parallel reduction, divider and internal-resistance numericals rotate yearly.
